To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the low E:P diet, compared to the diet with the NRC ( 1994) recommendation, increases carcass and breast yields at 43 and especially at 57 d, and abdominal fat pad weight at 57 d.
the optimal E to P ratio, for maximal breast meat yields, for broiler chicks may be lower than the NRC (1984) recommendations.
a low dietary E:P ratio increased the breast meat yield of male broiler chickens, and that this effect was more pronounced at 57 than 43 d of ages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of dietary energy and protein levels on the yields of carcass, breast and abdominal fat pads of broiler chicks at two different ages.
the effects of dietary energy and protein levels on carcass yield of broiler chickens.
the effects of dietary E:P ratio on growth and body composition of broilers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the optimal dietary E:P ratio for breast meat yield is lower than the NRC ( 1994 ) recommendation, but the magnitude of the difference depends on the energy level of the diet and on the age of the bird.
the optimal E/P ratio is lower than the NRC (1977, 1994) recommendations and the optimal energy level is higher than the NRC recommendation.

the E:P ratio should be lowered to increase breast meat yield, particularly at 7 to 28 and 43 to 57 d of broiler age, and that the energy level should be raised to increase breast meat and carcass yield at 7 to14 and 43 to42 d of age.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a moderate excess of dietary protein and a high energy level in the diet, in combination, improve carcass and breast meat yields in broiler chicks.
the optimal E: P ratio is 1.0 to 1.1.
the low E:P ratios, in both experiments, improved feed efficiency, increased carcass yield at 57 d, increased breast meat yield at 57 but not 43 d, and decreased abdominal fat pad weight.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal E/P ratio for maximal breast yield is below the NRC recommendation.
the E:P ratio should be lower than the current recommendation for maximal breast meat production in broilers, particularly at 6 wk of age.
the E:P ratio should be lower than that recommended by NRC (1993) for maximal breast meat weight in broilers.
